sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Export and delete account flow
sections.what: Tests that a user can download their data without passwords, that the delete button needs the exact typed word, and that the deleted account can no longer sign in. It also checks that the delete API refuses a wrong confirmation.
sections.why: Confirms the two privacy features work end to end, including the safety step that stops accidental deletion.
sections.watch_out: This test permanently removes the account it creates, so it must never point at a production database.

summary: Browser test that exports a user's data as a file, then deletes the account after typing a confirmation word and checks that sign-in no longer works.
purpose: Verifies two privacy rights: a user can download their own data, and a user can permanently delete their account.
why: Data export and account deletion are legal and trust requirements, so they need a test that runs the full path.
how: It creates a new user, signs in, opens the settings page and clicks the download link. It parses the file and checks the email matches and that no password hash appears. Then it confirms the delete button stays disabled until the exact word DELETE is typed, clicks it, and expects a redirect. Finally it tries to sign in again and expects an invalid credentials message. A second test checks the delete API rejects a wrong confirmation and that the export endpoint still works.
inputs: A new user created through the helpers, the signed-in browser page, and the settings page.
outputs: Pass or fail results. The export file is read and checked but not kept.
risks: The test deletes the account it creates, so it must run against a test database. A wrong database target could remove real rows.
debug: If the export check fails, look at the exported file and confirm the user record is present and free of password data. If deletion fails, check the confirmation field and the redirect. If sign-in still works after deletion, the delete path did not remove the account.
